clue.text: Decorated old woman at match embarrassed about nothing

indicators.note: the woman-and-embarrassed pair is wrapped about the zero, holding it within

parts.note: a bride is the woman at a wedding, a match in the marrying sense
O is the zero figure, nothing
an embarrassed face goes red

explanation.surface: A wedding guest blushes over a scoreless game while wearing a fancy outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks sporting and 'nothing' a nil score, but the match is a marriage. 'Old' belongs with the definition: this is the archaic form of embroidered.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic synonym: to broider was the older word for embellishing cloth with needlework.

clue.text: Prohibition on very loud Canadian resort

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A noise ban at a holiday spot in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff is a mountain town in Alberta, a well-known ski and national-park resort.

clue.text: Port's beginning to drop floating structure, causing a financial problem

indicators.note: in a down clue the port's opening letter drops, sinking to the bottom of its name

parts.note: Dover is the Channel port in Kent
a raft is a simple floating platform

explanation.surface: A harbour starting to lower a floating platform runs into money trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is the English Channel ferry port; 'beginning to drop' works because this is a down clue, so the first letter falls to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overdrawn at the bank, spending beyond the balance, is a common money worry.

clue.text: Drug that is suspect makes one deeply agitated

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or unreliable, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Someone who suspects a dodgy drug becomes very anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as a doubtful drug, but it asks for DRUGTHATIS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct synonym: someone frantic with worry or grief is described as beside themselves.

clue.text: Check made by engineers on regular beat?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
a pulse is a regular throb or beat

explanation.surface: Engineers carrying out a routine check on a steady rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' is a verb here: to drive back or halt an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or drive back an advance, as a defending army does, is to stop it in its tracks.

clue.text: Valley outside the borders of my French estate

indicators.note: the valley word sits outside, forming the borders around the French word

parts.note: a dene is a narrow wooded valley
mes is French for my before a plural noun

explanation.surface: A French landowner describes a valley lying beyond his estate's boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal and historical term for land held and worked by its owner, the grounds of a manor.

clue.text: No time for homely fashions

indicators.note: no time means the time letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: homely in the sense of unpretentious, simple, means modest

explanation.surface: Busy people have no time for comfortable, homely clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homely fashions' looks like a phrase; 'for' is just a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ways or styles of doing something, including trends in dress, are synonyms.

clue.text: One has ditchwater? There's nothing that's dull about it!

indicators.note: the word for dull goes about the zero, enclosing it

parts.note: mat (or matt) describes a dull, non-shiny finish
O is the zero figure

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about ditchwater, famously dull, and what lies around it.
explanation.walkthrough: Plays on the phrase 'dull as ditchwater', but dullness is in the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive ditch around a castle is filled with water, so it literally holds ditchwater.

clue.text: Girl with poem in the tube

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A girl reciting poetry on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The tube' suggests London's Underground, but it is an electronic valve.
explanation.definitionFit: An early electronic valve with two electrodes was a vacuum tube passing current one way.

clue.text: Modern music on sound system in street party, a form of torture

indicators.note: the music and sound system go inside the street-and-party pair

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the music above the sound system

parts.note: rap is a modern music genre
PA, public address, is a sound system

explanation.surface: Loud rap through speakers at a street party feels like torture.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical punishment in which the victim was hoisted by the arms and dropped with a jerk.

clue.text: Demands pounds in speech

indicators.note: spoken out, the word sounds like the one to enter

parts.note: to knead dough is to pound and work it

explanation.surface: Someone demanding money in pounds while talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like money; it is the verb, as with dough.
explanation.definitionFit: As nouns or verbs, requirements and necessities are what a person must have.

clue.text: Humourless politician with a stern style a bit like Trump's?

parts.note: po, as in po-faced, means humourless and disapproving
MP is a Member of Parliament
dour means stern and severe

explanation.surface: A grim, unsmiling politician whose hairdo resembles Donald Trump's.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle swept up high off the forehead, as Trump's swept-back quiff resembles.

clue.text: Politician and tennis player, without hesitation the top celebrities

indicators.note: the tennis star's name loses the hesitation sound

parts.note: Roger Federer is the Swiss tennis champion
er is the sound of hesitation
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A politician and a tennis star mingle with the A-list without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of central government over states, like Hamilton and Madison in US history.

clue.text: Water's about to ooze

indicators.note: about here signals turning the word round, back to front

parts.note: to pass water is to pee, so water's gives pees

explanation.surface: Water is about to ooze through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'soon to'; 'about' turns PEES round and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that leaks slowly through a porous material is trickling out, a synonym.

clue.text: Cleaning mess — what's humiliating about that?

indicators.note: the word for humiliating goes about, around, the mess

parts.note: shaming means humiliating
poo is a mess, as from a dog

explanation.surface: Cleaning up a mess, and the embarrassment that goes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing hair or carpets with a cleansing lather is a form of cleaning.

clue.text: Height certain to collect rubbish

indicators.note: the word for certain collects, takes in, the rubbish

parts.note: sure means certain
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone tall is sure to be asked to gather the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's natural standing height is their stature, also used for standing or reputation.

clue.text: Breakaway meeting involving London's financial district?

indicators.note: the meeting involves, takes inside, the district

parts.note: a session is a meeting or sitting
EC is the postcode area of the City of London, its financial centre

explanation.surface: A rebel faction meeting in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal withdrawal from a federation or union, like the Southern US states in 1861.

clue.text: Untidy heap containing red, decomposing shrub

indicators.note: one jumbled word contains the other
an untidy heap is in a mess, so its letters are disordered
decomposing means breaking up, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A compost heap with red bits of a rotting bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'Untidy' works on heap and 'decomposing' on red, and 'containing' puts the second jumble inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of jointed, near-leafless desert plants, source of the drug ephedrine.

clue.text: Poser of threat, desperate fellow? Foreigner no longer our enemy

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the strongman of the British comic The Dandy
Germany was Britain's wartime enemy, now an ally

explanation.surface: A frightening, desperate man, a foreigner, but now on our side.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a big-chinned cowboy in the long-running British children's comic The Dandy. Danger Man was also a 1960s British spy series.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone posing a threat is a hazardous individual, literally a perilous person.

clue.text: Work extra hard after holiday to produce something old and saucy?

definitions.meaning: to clear a backlog of tasks after a break
an old spelling of the tomato sauce ketchup

explanation.surface: Overtime after a break yields something old and cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a phrasal verb for clearing a backlog and an archaic spelling of the tomato condiment.

clue.text: Malleable president finally in charge

parts.note: last means finally

explanation.surface: A pliable president at last takes command.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easily moulded or shaped is pliable, the original sense before the material.

clue.text: Singer is good in loose cloak

indicators.note: good goes in the cloak word

parts.note: a domino is a loose hooded masquerade cloak

explanation.surface: A singer performing well in a flowing cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Plácido Domingo is the Spanish operatic tenor, one of the Three Tenors.

clue.text: One enthralled by left-winger repeatedly turning up as a mocker

indicators.note: the single letter is held captive within the doubled word
in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from the bottom upward
repeatedly means the left-winger is written twice

parts.note: a red is a communist, a left-winger
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone captivated by a radical leftist who keeps showing up, scoffing.
explanation.walkthrough: REDRED turned round gives DERDER, with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: One who ridicules or scoffs at others is a jeerer, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Knowing about a murder

indicators.note: the word for knowing goes about, around, the a

parts.note: sly can mean knowing, as in a sly look

explanation.surface: Someone who knows something about a murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A murder' looks like a noun; the definition is the verb 'murder'.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill violently, a literary synonym for killing.

clue.text: Conductors with no love for the mountains

indicators.note: with no love means the zero letter is removed

parts.note: anodes are electrodes, conductors of current
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: Orchestra conductors with no affection for the mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The great South American mountain range, the longest continental chain on Earth.

clue.text: Their horses are in front, running a bit closer

indicators.note: running suggests movement, so the letters are set in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: Racehorses ahead, the contest running ever closer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like racing, but describes horse-drawn carriages pulled from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Light two-wheeled hooded carriages drawn by a single horse, hitched ahead of the vehicle.

clue.text: Rich man making appeal for help, having hoarded gold

indicators.note: the appeal for help hoards, keeps inside, the gold

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A wealthy man pleading for help despite his stash of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: George Soros is the billionaire financier and philanthropist.

clue.text: Examination less than barely adequate

indicators.note: less than the full word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: scant means barely sufficient

explanation.surface: A test result that falls below even a bare pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A close look or medical imaging test is a scrutiny, as in a brain scan.

clue.text: Shown to be exonerated, five released

indicators.note: the five letter is released, let go from the word

parts.note: vindicated means cleared of blame
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Five prisoners released after being cleared of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed out or signalled, as a sign or gauge does, a past participle synonym.

clue.text: Turkish community is said to adjoin old Russian community

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: the clue word is, spoken, has a buzzing final sound
a mir was a peasant commune in Tsarist Russia

explanation.surface: A Turkish town reportedly bordering an old Russian village.
explanation.definitionFit: A major port city on Turkey's Aegean coast, formerly Smyrna.

clue.text: Month in which car manufacturer lays off workers, finally

indicators.note: lays off means lets go one letter of the maker's name

parts.note: Nissan is the Japanese car maker

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of workers

explanation.surface: A month when a carmaker makes staff redundant at last.
explanation.definitionFit: The first month of the Jewish religious calendar, in spring, when Passover falls.

clue.text: Vital chaps who help rulers

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the people who help rulers

parts.note: core means vital, central, as in core values
gents are men, chaps

explanation.surface: Essential men who assist those in power.
explanation.definitionFit: Those ruling jointly alongside a monarch share authority, assisting the sovereign.
